content.rendered:
The first time Bruce Springsteen played “The Last Time” was in Atlanta in 1978. (It’s a terrible recording, though, so I’ll spare you from listening to it.)

The next time Bruce played “The Last Time” was the very last night of the Darkness Tour–New Years Day, 1979. (That recording is just fine.)

But the best time Bruce played “The Last Time” was… well, the last time.

On October 9, 2009, Bruce bid farewell to Giants Stadium (soon to meet the wrecking ball) by honoring an inspired fan request during the encore of his 24th and final concert at that storied venue.

The Rolling Stones, of course, have played “The Last Time” lots of times. It’s their song, after all, reaching #9 on the Billboard Hot 100 in the U.S. and topping the UK Singles chart upon its release in 1965.

Well, it’s sort of their song–they adapted it from a 1958 recording by The Staple Singers, who adapted theirs from a traditional song that goes back a lot further (and further forward, I guess, since there’s that whole “Bittersweet Symphony” brouhaha as well).

As for Bruce, it seems he’s played “The Last Time” for the last time.

Until the next time.

The Last Time
First performed: October 1, 1978 (Atlanta, GA)
Last performed: October 9, 2009 (East Rutherford, NJ)

© July 24, 2020

excerpt.rendered: Watch Bruce send Giants Stadium off to meet the wrecking ball with an appropriately timed cover of one of The Rolling Stones’ earliest hits.

jetpack-related-posts.title: (I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Mick Jagger on stage at the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame for one of the very first songs Bruce ever covered in concert.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Down the Road Apiece
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: From Bruce's pre-E Street Days to just pre-pandemic, "Down the Road Apiece" has always been an epic, crowd-pleasing jam. Let's watch and listen to some of the best inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: December 15
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: On this date: Winterland '78. Need I say more? (Okay, how about a Rolling Stones guest appearance and the streaming video release of Springsteen on Broadway?)

jetpack-related-posts.title: Not Fade Away
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: Bruce covered "Not Fade Away" as far back as 1971 and as recently as last summer. It's always at the ready for an impromptu team-up--watch some of best ones inside.

jetpack-related-posts.title: Dead Flowers
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Steve Earle for a faithful cover of The Rolling Stones’ country rock classic, “Dead Flowers.”

jetpack-related-posts.title: I Just Want to Make Love to You
jetpack-related-posts.author: Ken
jetpack-related-posts.excerpt: One time only: Bruce joins Danny Clinch and the Tangiers Blues Band for an eight-minute jam to Willie Dixon's early classic.
